obligations.text: On Unix, every input file and store item the Node binding's filesystem host reads is opened with `O_NONBLOCK` (store items also with `O_NOFOLLOW`) through `rustev_surface::host::open_input`, so a FIFO or device swapped in after the metadata check opens at once and is refused by the check on the handle; no read through that host waits for a FIFO writer.
The CLI and the Node host share one implementation of the non-blocking open; the CLI's `rustev_cli::io::open_input` behavior (006 3.3.1) is unchanged.

A Unix test creates a FIFO with no writer at an input path and at a store item, and asserts that the Node host's read returns the not-a-regular-file refusal (input) or `Inaccessible` (store item) within a bounded time instead of blocking.

sectionHeadings: 069: The Node binding's filesystem host opens inputs without blocking (amends 006, 027 and 067)
3.4 What the amended specs now say
record.summary: An amendment of approved specs 067 (3.4.2 and its implementation record's residual race), 027 (the Node binding's host) and 006 (3.3.1's non-blocking open, which moves to a shared home), for #566, ratified by the owner on 2026-11-08 (A-89). The Node binding's filesystem host for `engine.liveRun` opens every input file and store item with the standard library's blocking open, so a regular file swapped for a FIFO or device between its metadata check and the open can block the call; the CLI closes that window with a non-blocking open. This spec moves the CLI's open into `rustev-surface`, has the CLI and the Node host both use it, and requires a test that a FIFO at an input path or store item is refused without blocking. Nothing read changes: the check on the open handle already refused a non-regular file.
